cards.text: The fight against Midian is on, and Gideon is right in the middle of it. Then the men of Ephraim, one of Israel's tribes, march up to him. And friend, they did NOT come to say congratulations.

cards.question: What has the men of Ephraim so upset with Gideon?

answers.text: He didn't call them to fight Midian
He kept the plunder for himself
He put Manasseh in charge of them

cards.question: The men of Ephraim bring their complaint to Gideon calmly and quietly.

cards.text: Gideon could fire right back at them. Instead, he's got angry men in his face, and he answers them with a question about GRAPES.

cards.question: Gideon tells Ephraim their leftover grapes beat the whole grape harvest of Abiezer, his own clan. What is Gideon saying?

answers.text: Ephraim did more than he did

cards.text: Then he reminds them that God delivered Oreb and Zeeb, the two princes of Midian, into THEIR hand. That's somebody yelling at you for leaving them off the group chat, and you reply, “Are you kidding? This chat is DEAD without you.”

cards.question: Once Gideon gives the men of Ephraim the credit, their anger against him ___.

cards.text: Now Gideon and his three hundred men cross the Jordan, and they're STILL chasing. They come to the town of Succoth.

cards.question: Gideon asks the men of Succoth for ___ because his troops are ___.

cards.text: He tells them he's still chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian. Two KINGS, friend, chased down by three hundred guys who'd trade their swords for one cookie right now.

cards.question: The leaders of Succoth are happy to feed Gideon's tired men.

cards.text: They ask, “Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession, that we should give bread to your army?” That's asking your boss for a pen and hearing, “Finish the project FIRST, then we'll talk about pens.”

cards.question: Gideon answers Succoth with a warning for when the LORD hands him the two kings. What does he say he'll do to them?

answers.text: Tear their flesh with thorns and briers
Burn their whole city to the ground
Take away all their flocks and herds

cards.text: From there Gideon goes up to Penuel and asks them for bread too. Friend, I bet he's thinking, surely THIS town has a heart.

cards.question: How do the men of Penuel answer Gideon's request for his troops?

answers.text: They refuse him just like Succoth
They give his men bread and water
They send men to join the chase

cards.question: Gideon has a warning for Penuel too. What does he say he'll tear down when he returns in triumph?

cards.text: Meanwhile, Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian, are in Karkor with about fifteen thousand men. That's all that's left of the armies of the people of the east. Fifteen thousand is the LEFTOVERS, friend.

cards.question: Only about fifteen thousand men are left. How many swordsmen from the armies of the east have already fallen?

cards.text: Then Gideon goes up by the caravan route east of Nobah and Jogbehah. Fifteen thousand men are out there, and the three hundred guys nobody would even give bread to are the ones doing the CHASING.

cards.question: Gideon's attack on the army at Karkor takes them by surprise.
When Zebah and Zalmunna flee, what happens to the two kings of Midian?

cards.text: And their entire army is routed. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and even I never had a day that bad.
On his way back along the Ascent of Heres, Gideon captures a young man from Succoth and questions him. Remember Succoth? Oh, Gideon remembers Succoth.

cards.question: The young man writes down for Gideon the ___ of Succoth's seventy-seven leaders and elders.

cards.text: Then Gideon walks into Succoth and says, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me,” and he brings up their question about the kings' hands. Ever lose an argument and walk back in later with the receipts? Gideon's receipts are two KINGS.

cards.question: Gideon warned Succoth back when they refused him bread. Now what does he do to the elders of the city?

answers.text: Disciplines them with thorns and briers
Forgives them and goes on his way
Makes them carry all his supplies

cards.question: Gideon leaves the tower of Penuel standing.

cards.text: He pulls down the tower of Penuel and kills the men of the city. Next, Gideon asks Zebah and Zalmunna, “What kind of men did you kill at Tabor?”

cards.question: How do Zebah and Zalmunna describe the men they killed at Tabor?
The kings say those men were like Gideon, “each one resembling the son of a king.” Gideon tells them the men killed at Tabor were his ___.

cards.text: Then Gideon tells them, “As surely as the LORD lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you.”

cards.question: When Gideon tells Jether, his firstborn son, to kill the kings, Jether draws his sword.

cards.text: Jether does not draw his sword, because he's fearful and still a youth. Friend, the oven timer makes ME jump, so I am not judging.

cards.question: Zebah and Zalmunna tell Gideon, “Get up and kill us yourself, for as the man is, so is his strength.” What do they mean?

answers.text: Killing them takes a grown man's strength
Kings should only die by a king's hand
Gideon is weaker than his own son

cards.text: So Gideon kills Zebah and Zalmunna himself and takes the crescent ornaments from the necks of their camels. That's where we stop for now, friend, but trust me, Gideon's story is NOT done.

findings.problem: Story cards 1, 7 and 9 each contain three sentences. None is the walkthrough's opening card, so each is limited to one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The correct answer is the only four-word option and is noticeably longer than the two two-word distractors, making it stand out from the other answers.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The question and answer say Gideon disciplines the elders of the city with thorns and briers. Judges 8:16 instead says he took the elders and disciplined the men of Succoth, so the card changes who receives the discipline.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
